title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Suncrest Logistics
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing for Dedicated + extra region by 2026-12-14
Jordan to share benchmark results for 1k qps load test by 2026-12-10
Customer to confirm procurement timeline and legal redlines by 2026-12-16
action_items: Maya Patel — send amended SOW with 12-month extension and APAC region add-on — 2026-12-14
Jordan Lee — run nightly KV-cache focused benchmark and share raw results — 2026-12-10
Priya Mehta — share final list of production routes and expected p95 latency targets — 2026-12-13
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Customer is evaluating a capacity upgrade to Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and adding APAC region for lower latency to their Asian hubs. Discussed pricing impact, latency vs cost tradeoffs, SOC2 & VPC requirements, and timeline for contract extension. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide updated pricing and benchmark results; customer to provide production route list and procurement timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Priya, Liam, Diego, Sofia — thanks for making time. We'll run about 45 minutes. Jordan from our infra team and Asha our CSM are on.
[00:12] Priya Mehta: Hi Maya, morning. Quick agenda — renewal terms, capacity increase for next quarter, and adding APAC region.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Also wanna go over benchmarks, we saw a couple of tail latencies last month so want to make sure Dedicated will fix that.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Yeah hi all — can do, I'll run through latency profiles and how Dedicated + APAC peering will change things.
[00:32] Diego Alvarez: Quick note from infra — we need VPC peering and KMS support; our security team flagged key rotation and audit logs.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Totally, we'll cover security. Before we start, just to confirm current contract ends end of Jan, right Sofia?
[00:46] Sofia Ramos: Correct, current term ends 2027-01-31 and procurement prefers to have approved paper by mid-December.
[00:52] Maya Patel: Great, that's helpful. Okay Jordan, can you summarize what Dedicated would give them vs hosted?
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Sure. So Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictability in throughput, lower p95 under load because you avoid noisy neighbor and can tune batching. Also enables pinning model versions. From our end, we can provide autoscaling within the pool but you get guaranteed baseline capacity. For Suncrest I'd recommend a 2-node reserved pool to start for their peak routes, then autoscale to burst capacity as needed.
[01:21] Liam O'Connor: When you say p95 improvements, are we looking like 50-100ms improvements or more? Our p95 for generation spikes to 1.2s under heavy job loads.
[01:32] Jordan Lee: We saw similar in other logistics customers. For your workload mix (short routing prompts + some 2k token summaries) Dedicated plus prefix caching can typically bring p95 down from ~1.2s to ~650-800ms depending on batching. If we move heavy inference routes to an APAC region for your Asia hubs, you further reduce network RTT which could shave another 60-120ms.
[01:55] Priya Mehta: That sounds promising, what's the cost delta?
[02:00] Maya Patel: We'll put numbers in the updated SOW — depends on node types and commit length. Jordan, for a 2-node pool estimate vs hosted on demand?
[02:09] Jordan Lee: Ballpark: Dedicated reserved about 1.6-1.9x the unit cost of hosted at baseline, but because of unit efficiency and reduced tail latency you often see better per-effective-request economics. If they commit 12 months versus month-to-month, we can offer a discount tier — I'll outline 12 vs 24 month pricing scenarios in the follow-up.
[02:29] Diego Alvarez: A couple sec on networking — we run everything in a VPC and require customer-managed peering; can Redwood support SAML SSO for admin console and IAM roles integration?
[02:41] Asha Kumar: Yes, we support SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC. For VPC peering we provide guided setup; for on-prem we have extra steps but for VPC we do managed peering and private link. KMS: we support customer KMS/HSM integration for key rotation.
[02:58] Sofia Ramos: And SOC2 compliance? Our auditors will need certs and evidence.
[03:02] Maya Patel: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll attach the compliance pack, and Jordan will include audit log retention options.
[03:10] Priya Mehta: On the APAC region, which cloud regions do you support? We need Tokyo and Singapore ideally.
[03:17] Jordan Lee: We currently have hosted endpoints in Singapore and Tokyo regions. For Dedicated/APAC we can provision in Singapore fast, Tokyo might be a short lead time for reserved pools — say 3-4 weeks. If you need immediate lower latency, we can apply routing rules to route Asia-origin requests to the nearest hosted endpoint in Singapore while we spin up Dedicated in Tokyo.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: Ok, routing fallbacks are fine. One concern: we use quantized model variants in prod to reduce cost — will Dedicated support Q4-bit runtimes and our current model artifacts? We use a compressed LLM from internal repo.
[03:50] Jordan Lee: Our runtime supports widely used quant formats, and we have a model onboarding path; we'll need to validate your artifact, could be some kernel tuning required. For custom artifacts we do a short onboarding POC — typically 1-2 weeks to validate inference profile.
[04:05] Priya Mehta: If onboarding takes 1-2 weeks, does that block the renewal? Procurement wants to sign before year end.
[04:12] Maya Patel: Not necessarily. We can put model onboarding as an action post-sign and include a clause for a 30-45 day onboarding milestone. The contract can include credits if onboarding delays occur.
[04:22] Diego Alvarez: What about data residency — logs and request traces — can we keep logs in our VPC or have a retention window?
[04:29] Asha Kumar: Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via push exports; retention windows are configurable. For request-level logs we can do redaction and store minimal metadata per your retention policy; we can also disable storage except for error traces.
[04:44] Sofia Ramos: Pricing question — if we add APAC as an add-on, is it billed as an extra reserved pool or an incremental region fee?
[04:51] Maya Patel: Typically it's another reserved pool in that region. We can do a multi-region bundle discount if you commit to 12 or 24 months. We'll show scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[05:02] Liam O'Connor: Jordan, about benchmarks — last month our nightly spike caused batching to go odd and we saw KV-cache misses. Can you simulate our mix?
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, please share an anonymized sample of your route distribution and sequence length histogram. I'll run a 24-hour soak with your distribution. I'll enable KV-cache warmup to see steady-state. Expect results in ~48-72 hours depending on size.
[05:22] Priya Mehta: We can pull samples — we'll share before Friday.
[05:25] Maya Patel: Great. Also, on contract length — what incentives for 24 month vs 12 month?
[05:30] Jordan Lee: Bigger discounts, lower overage rates, and we can lock in kernel optimization support commitment for model variants you pin. For 24 months we can also include a reserved headroom and preferential capacity during bursts.
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: Our security team also asked about pen tests and third party audits. Do you allow yearly attestation or do we have to use your certs?
[05:52] Asha Kumar: We provide SOC2 reports and support allowing third-party pentests on the VPC overlay endpoints; for hosted endpoints we do not permit pentests on shared infra but for Dedicated we can coordinate.
[06:04] Priya Mehta: One more — latency SLOs. We need p95 under 900ms for critical routes. Is that reasonable with Dedicated + APAC?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Based on the numbers you gave, yes — with Dedicated + APAC peering + KV caching warmed, target p95 <900ms is achievable. We'll validate in the soak test. If we miss SLA we can include credits in the SOW.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. Any blockers on procurement/contract side? Sofia?
[06:28] Sofia Ramos: Need pricing, SOW, and security pack by next week. Also need legal to review data processing addendum — they want to see KMS terms and subprocessor list.
[06:37] Maya Patel: We'll include that. Quick question on rollout — if we do APAC, can we do a canary route approach?
[06:43] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can do canary by route and model version. We support traffic splits and automatic fallback to hosted region if Dedicated capacity is strained.
[06:52] Priya Mehta: Regarding canary, how do you handle quality regressions between quantized and full precision variants?
[06:59] Jordan Lee: We provide eval tooling and can run diff-evals on sample prompt sets. We can also do shadow testing so you can verify no regressions before switching traffic.
[07:10] Diego Alvarez: Ops question — who owns autoscaling rules? We need to align with our internal autoscaling triggers to avoid double autoscale.
[07:17] Asha Kumar: You own your app-level autoscaling triggers; Redwood's autoscaling within Dedicated handles infra scaling inside the pool. We can coordinate a handoff policy and provide hooks to your telemetry for scaling signals.
[07:29] Maya Patel: Good. Any other concerns?
[07:32] Liam O'Connor: Only that the model artifact validation mustn't change semantics — we need a signed-off acceptance test.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: We'll supply an acceptance test harness and host the tests, and we'll require both runs to pass before promoting to prod.
[07:45] Priya Mehta: Timeline recap?
[07:47] Maya Patel: Sure — Maya to send updated pricing and SOW with APAC add-on and contract options by 2026-12-14. Jordan to run benchmarks and share results by 2026-12-10. Customer to provide production route list and sample distributions by 2026-12-09. Procurement to review and revert legal redlines by 2026-12-16.
[08:04] Sofia Ramos: That works for procurement.
[08:06] Maya Patel: Anything else — if not we'll close and follow up via email.
[08:10] Priya Mehta: No, thank you. That clarifies the path forward.
[08:13] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone.
[08:15] Maya Patel: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the sheet.
[45:00] <end of call>

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hears (Red wood vs Redwood, KV-cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash), filler words, and overlapping talk on a few points. References to artifacts: "updated SOW" (link: /redwood/sow/suncrest-dedicated-draft-v2), "security pack" (link: /redwood/security/suncrest-pack.zip), benchmark spreadsheet (link: /redwood/benchmarks/suncrest-load-2026-12-07.xlsx).
